settings.title: Default view for compatible agents
settings.subtitle: Automatically switch to chat as soon as Ghostex detects that an agent session supports it.

settings.title: Close empty sessions when starting a new one
settings.subtitle: When you start a new session, close this project's other sessions that have nothing typed, drafted or queued. Only applies when Chat is the default view for that agent; with Terminal it never runs.

settings.title: Custom transcript width (set with Transcript width)
settings.subtitle: On once Transcript width is dragged to a percentage; off keeps Auto, where the transcript matches the prompt composer's width.

settings.title: Transcript width
settings.subtitle: The centered transcript's width on wide panes. Auto matches the prompt composer; drag to set a percentage of the pane instead. The prompt composer keeps its standard width either way unless Chat box matches transcript width is on.

settings.title: Show file edit previews
settings.subtitle: Show the first seven code lines in each file edit. Turn off to show only the path and change counts.

settings.title: Tool call cards (preview)
settings.subtitle: Show each run of tool calls as one line that says which call is running now; click it to see every call with its result, time and the reason for any failure. Off keeps the current look. Agent work's Reduced and Quiet replace these cards.

settings.title: Message layout
settings.subtitle: Default puts your messages on the right as bubbles. Left aligned starts every message at the same left edge.

settings.title: Your messages
settings.subtitle: How your messages stand out from the agent's: Default keeps the bubble, Band puts them on a soft full-width strip. Band also left-aligns them.

settings.title: Agent work
settings.subtitle: Default shows a Worked for card before each reply. Reduced shows one small line for everything the agent did for each of your messages. Quiet keeps the agent's work out of the chat and puts a button for it with each reply's hover buttons.

settings.title: Status line in the chat
settings.subtitle: Show what the agent is doing as the last line of the chat instead of above the chat box.

settings.title: Chat box matches transcript width
settings.subtitle: When Transcript width is set to a percentage, the chat box takes the same width instead of its standard width.

settings.title: Message spacing
settings.subtitle: Compact puts messages closer together and keeps a small row under each message for its buttons, which show on hover.

settings.title: Default to Detailed view
settings.subtitle: New chats open in Detailed view, with the work under each agent reply shown. Off, they open in Normal view. More actions > View in a chat picks Summary, Normal or Detailed for that chat.

settings.title: Keep chat box expanded while scrolling
settings.subtitle: Keep the desktop chat box at full size while you scroll the transcript instead of shrinking it as you scroll up and growing it back at the end.

settings.title: Press Escape twice to interrupt
settings.subtitle: While the agent is working, the first Escape asks you to press Escape again within 2 seconds before it interrupts. Turn off to interrupt on the first Escape.

settings.title: Catch me up button
settings.subtitle: Show a Catch me up button at the top right of the chat box while it is empty. It has your Title Generation Agent (a small, cheap model) read the session's last 30 agent messages and shows where the session stands: what needs you, what is done, in progress or untested.

settings.title: Send when you pick an answer
settings.subtitle: When a question card asks one question, picking an answer sends it right away, without Send answers. Cards with several questions, multiple-choice questions, Other and text answers still wait for Send.

settings.title: Wait for turn end before sending form answers
settings.subtitle: Send answers from Ghostex forms and Ghostex pages only after the agent finishes its turn. Off sends them like a normal chat message, which the agent can read after its current tool call finishes.

settings.title: Open Ghostex pages in
settings.subtitle: Where a Ghostex page (gx page) an agent shows in chat, such as a mockup or a comparison, opens when you click its card: a popup over the chat, the Files view, or your default web browser. Answers you send from the page reach the agent the same way in all three. The phone always opens pages in its own viewer.

settings.title: Coordinator board opens as
settings.subtitle: What the Board pill above a coordinator's chat box opens: its lines of work as a list beside the chat, or as columns over the chat, one per group. The switch at the top of either view changes this too.

settings.title: Tell agents about Ghostex
settings.subtitle: Agent sessions Ghostex starts get a short note that they run in Ghostex: it can show Ghostex pages, forms and visuals in the chat, install Ghostex skills, and `ghostex agent-guide` explains the rest. Agents use it only when you ask for one of those things. Applies to sessions started or resumed after you change it.

settings.title: Every effort level in coordinator pickers
settings.subtitle: Also lists the levels above XHigh (Max, Ultra and the like) in the coordinator effort pickers, where the agent has them. Coordinators work best on High or XHigh.

settings.title: Playbook overrides
settings.subtitle: Your own instructions for every coordinator, such as "Never push without asking". Coordinators read them after Ghostex's playbook and follow them over it, and Ghostex's playbook keeps getting its updates. Existing coordinators follow them from their next message.

settings.title: Read aloud voice
settings.subtitle: The voice Read aloud speaks the agent's replies with: System voice, or one of the voices installed on this computer. Add voices in your computer's speech or accessibility settings. The phone has its own Voice in its Settings > Chat.

settings.title: Read aloud speed
settings.subtitle: How fast Read aloud speaks, from 0.75× to twice as fast. Ghostex in a browser uses it too; the phone has its own Speed.

settings.title: Read aloud
settings.subtitle: Read aloud can't speak on this computer, so it has no controls here. It works in the Ghostex phone app and in Ghostex in a browser connected to this computer.

settings.title: Claude task list
settings.subtitle: Turn on Claude's task list tools, so Claude can keep a checklist that the Session details panel shows. Recent Claude models only get them when Ghostex asks. Applies to Claude sessions started or woken after you change it. Shown while the Session details panel extension is on.

settings.title: Marked handovers in every session
settings.subtitle: Coordinators and their threads start each part of the message they hand back with a marker such as ✅ Done or 🧪 Untested, and end it with what needs you (⚠️ Read this, 🛑 Blocked, 💡 Suggestions, ❓ Needs you), so you never miss it. Turn this on to have every other agent session do the same. Applies to sessions started or resumed after you change it.

settings.title: Show marker emojis
settings.subtitle: Not recommended. Show the marker emoji (❓ ✅ ⚠️ and the rest) at the start of each coloured section, in every style. Off: the colour and the label show the kind. Shown while Marked handovers is on.

settings.title: Marked sections style
settings.subtitle: How the chat colours the sections an agent marks: coloured labels, a thin left rule, or a coloured badge in place of the emoji. Shown while Marked handovers is on.

settings.title: Heading colour strength
settings.subtitle: How strongly the coloured section headings in agents' handovers (Done, Needs you, Untested and the rest) stand out. 100% is full colour; lower values blend the headings toward the normal text colour, and 0% leaves them in plain bold text.

settings.title: Coordinators answer without markers
settings.subtitle: Not recommended. Coordinators answer normally, without marking the sections of their handovers. Their threads still mark the reports they send to the coordinator. Applies to coordinators started or resumed after you change it.

settings.title: Preset
settings.subtitle: Apply a sidebar UI preset or show Custom when controlled settings diverge.

settings.title: Sidebar
settings.subtitle: Project sidebar lists each project with its sessions under it. Unified sidebar shows every session in one list, with the ones that need you on top. Both show every connected computer together unless Separate by machine is on.

settings.title: Separate by machine
settings.subtitle: Show one computer at a time, each with its own tab, project list and Spaces. Off (the default): one list for every connected computer, where a project on several computers is one entry with the sessions of all of them, and Spaces and project groups are shared by all of them.

settings.title: Merge copies of the same repository
settings.subtitle: Show two folders on this computer that are copies of the same repository (the same git remote, opened at the same folder inside it) as one project, with the sessions of both. Turn off to give each folder its own project with only its own sessions. Copies on different computers are one project either way. The phone follows this. Shown while Separate by machine is off.

settings.title: Moving section
settings.subtitle: Fold sessions whose agent is working or still running something in the background into a Moving section at the bottom of the list. They return to the top of the list when they need you. Shown while the Unified sidebar is selected.

settings.title: Group by project
settings.subtitle: Put every machine's sessions of one repository under one header, with its Moving, Snoozed and Parked sections inside it. Drag the headers to arrange them. Drafts stay above the groups. Also in the sidebar's Sort & Filter menu. Shown while the Unified sidebar is selected.

settings.title: When switching to a Space
settings.subtitle: Reopen the session you last had open in a Space when you switch to it, in the view its project was in. Shown while the Spaces extension is on.

settings.title: Switch Space when opening a session from another Space
settings.subtitle: Switch the selected Space to the one that owns a session you open from outside it, such as through Back/Forward or Search by Prompt. Shown while the Spaces extension is on.

settings.title: Keep the last project running for
settings.subtitle: After you switch to another project or Space, keep the terminals, chats, and view that were open in the previous project running for this many minutes so switching back is instant. 0 releases them right away. Keep views loaded (Auto Sleep) keeps every side panel view until its Auto Sleep time instead.

settings.title: Remember sidebar per view
settings.subtitle: Off: hiding the sidebar hides it everywhere. On: Agents and the wide views (Browser, Code, Files, Kanban, Automate) each keep their own open or hidden sidebar; the Commands pane follows the same split.

settings.title: Card details: project icons
settings.subtitle: Show project artwork or a square with the project’s first letter beside project names.

settings.title: Card details: agent icon
settings.subtitle: Hide session agent icons until a session row is hovered.

settings.title: Card details: browser favicon
settings.subtitle: Hide browser page favicons until a session row is hovered.

settings.title: Card details: last active time
settings.subtitle: Hide Last Active timestamps from session-card title rows.

settings.title: Highlight unanswered questions
settings.subtitle: Give sessions with a detected unanswered question a soft pink background, including while the agent keeps working. Currently supports Codex asynchronous questions.

settings.title: Card details: project git stats
settings.subtitle: Hide +added/-removed line counts in sidebar project rows.

settings.title: Card details: changed-file count
settings.subtitle: Show changed-file counts in sidebar project row git stats.

settings.title: Card details: untracked lines
settings.subtitle: Count untracked lines in a project's git stats when the tracked diff is +0 -0 (prompts like Starship ignore untracked lines).

settings.title: Animations (fold speed, set with Animations)
settings.subtitle: Set how quickly sidebar sections, groups, and projects expand or collapse, and how quickly the floating sidebar and Agents Panel slide in from the window edge. Set to 0 for no animation.

settings.title: Animations
settings.subtitle: Set how fast the sidebar, the side panel, the Agents Panel and the bottom or right panel slide open and closed: Off, Slow, Normal or Fast. Reduce Motion in your computer settings always turns it off.

settings.title: Close side panel with its last tab
settings.subtitle: Close the side panel when you close its last tab, instead of showing the Open a view picker.

settings.title: Session tooltips delay (set with Session tooltips)
settings.subtitle: Set how long sidebar hover labels wait before appearing. Set to 0 to show them immediately.

settings.title: Sidebar width on double-click
settings.subtitle: Width restored when double-clicking the sidebar resize handle.

settings.title: Commands pane height on double-click
settings.subtitle: Height used when opening the command pane and when double-clicking its top resize rail.

settings.title: Commands pane side
settings.subtitle: Dock the command pane below the workspace or to its right.

settings.title: Auto-minimize Commands pane
settings.subtitle: Minimize the Commands pane this long after you move focus elsewhere and the pointer leaves it. Commands keep running. Off keeps the pane open.

settings.title: Minimize after (set with Auto-minimize Commands pane)
settings.subtitle: How long the Commands pane stays open after focus and the pointer leave it.

settings.title: Hide projects without sessions
settings.subtitle: Leave projects with no sessions out of the Project sidebar, whatever state a session is in; the open project always stays, and a Show all projects row at the end of the list brings them back. Also in the sidebar's Sort & Filter menu.

settings.title: Worktree sessions show in their project
settings.subtitle: List a session started in a worktree under its repository's project, with the worktree's branch on its row, instead of giving the worktree a project of its own. The session still works in the worktree's folder. Turn off to show each worktree as its own project under its repository. Shown while the Project sidebar is selected.

settings.title: Pinned order
settings.subtitle: Keep pinned sessions in the order you drag them into, or put the pinned session that came back to you last (started, sent a message, or finished a turn) first. With Most recently updated, pinned sessions can't be dragged to rearrange them. Applies to both sidebars and the phone. Also in the sidebar's Sort & Filter menu.

settings.title: Group working sessions
settings.subtitle: Move sessions into a collapsed Working section under their project while their agent works; they return to Sessions when it stops or needs you. Also in the sidebar's Sort & Filter menu.

settings.title: Double-click empty sidebar space to create a session
settings.subtitle: Create a session from empty sidebar space.

settings.title: Enable session parking
settings.subtitle: Move deferred sessions into a collapsible Parked section at the bottom of the sidebar.

settings.title: Sleep session when parking
settings.subtitle: Sleep a session automatically when it is moved into the Parked section.

settings.title: Ask for a tag when parking or snoozing
settings.subtitle: Open the Tag as menu when a session is parked or snoozed so it can be tagged right away.

settings.title: Unpark after sending a message
settings.subtitle: Move a parked session out of the Parked section when you send it a message.

settings.title: Double-click session cards to rename
settings.subtitle: Makes clicking on a session respond a bit slower so we can detect the double click

settings.title: Session hover buttons (click to toggle, drag to reorder)
settings.subtitle: Buttons a session card shows when you hover it in the Project sidebar. Click an icon to turn it on or off; drag icons to reorder them. Buttons to the right of the chevron always show, buttons to its left hide until the chevron is clicked. By default the strip is Tag, Park, Sleep, chevron, Close. The button beside the strip copies the Unified sidebar's. Shown while the Project sidebar is selected.

settings.title: Session hover buttons (click to toggle, drag to reorder)
settings.subtitle: Buttons a session card shows when you hover it in the Unified sidebar, which keeps its own strip. Click an icon to turn it on or off; drag icons to reorder them. Buttons to the right of the chevron always show, buttons to its left hide until the chevron is clicked, and opening the chevron opens it on every card. By default the strip is Tag, Sleep, chevron, Snooze, Park, Close. The button beside the strip copies the Project sidebar's. Shown while the Unified sidebar is selected.

settings.title: Session links in the sidebar
settings.subtitle: How a session card shows the pull requests, issues and Linear tickets it is linked to. Always: a line of them under every card that has any. Selected session: that line only under the session you have open. Badge: a small count on the card, coloured by the most pressing one, grey once all are merged or closed. Open work only: a line of the ones still open, none once they are all merged or closed. Hovering a card with links shows them all in a card beside the sidebar, except with Off, which shows nothing.

settings.title: Title sessions by their branch
settings.subtitle: Name a session after the branch it works on, without your name and the ticket number (yahia/spx-1245-copy-link shows as copy-link), until you rename it yourself. Sessions on main keep their own title.

settings.title: Offer Clean up when a PR merges
settings.subtitle: When a session's pull request is merged, its card asks once whether to clean up (remove the session's worktree and park the session; a worktree with uncommitted changes is kept) or keep it.

settings.title: Hover buttons also in context menu
settings.subtitle: Also list the enabled hover buttons in the session right-click menu, in their usual place in the menu. Close is never listed while it is on the card. Turn off to leave every button out of the menu once it is on the card.

settings.title: Session tooltips
settings.subtitle: Show a tooltip with the full session name when you hover a session in the sidebar. Turn off to show none; other sidebar tooltips stay.

settings.title: Tag filter list
settings.subtitle: Add your own tags, then reorder, hide, disable, or delete tags and their separators for the sidebar and the Tag as menu.

settings.title: Dim sleeping sessions
settings.subtitle: Fade sleeping sessions in the sidebar so they stand apart from awake ones.

settings.title: Wake sleeping sessions when selected
settings.subtitle: Wake a sleeping session as soon as you select it. Turn off to open it with a Resume button instead, so switching sessions does not wake it by accident.

settings.title: Ghostty settings actions
settings.subtitle: Recommended terminal settings, Import from Ghostty (fonts and cursor, not the theme), the Ghostty app's config, Ghostex's own terminal config, Ghostty docs, and defaults.

settings.title: Terminal background
settings.subtitle: Only changes the terminal panes. Black / white is pure black in dark mode and pure white in light mode.

settings.title: Terminal background color
settings.subtitle: Custom terminal background, painted behind terminal text in dark and light mode.

settings.title: Background opacity (%)
settings.subtitle: How much of the work area's glass tint terminals keep while transparency is on (Settings > Interface > Transparency). 100% matches the rest of the work area; lower shows more of what is behind the window. Off while transparency is off.

settings.title: Background image
settings.subtitle: Absolute path to an image drawn behind terminal panes.

settings.title: Background image opacity
settings.subtitle: Blend the background image toward the terminal background color.

settings.title: Font weight
settings.subtitle: Set terminal text weight.

settings.title: Bold text uses a heavier font
settings.subtitle: Draw bold terminal text in a heavier weight. Turn off to keep bold text at your normal font weight, so it stands out by color only. A font-style-bold or font-variation-bold line in Ghostex's terminal config takes priority.

settings.title: Line height
settings.subtitle: Adjust terminal row height.

settings.title: Letter spacing
settings.subtitle: Adjust spacing between glyphs.

settings.title: Match chat width
settings.subtitle: Use the full pane, match the chat transcript, or set an independent terminal width.

settings.title: Terminal width (%)
settings.subtitle: Set the centered terminal body width as a percentage.

settings.title: Use this width in the Commands pane too
settings.subtitle: Apply the narrower terminal width to command pane terminals too.

settings.title: Padding
settings.subtitle: Add left and right inner padding inside the terminal content area.

settings.title: Vertical padding (set with Padding)
settings.subtitle: Add top and bottom inner padding inside the terminal content area.

settings.title: Cursor style
settings.subtitle: Choose the cursor shape.

settings.title: Cursor blink
settings.subtitle: Blink the terminal cursor.

settings.title: Keep sleeping tabs asleep until clicked
settings.subtitle: Select sleeping pane tabs without waking them until the empty pane is clicked.

settings.title: Model picker in terminal view
settings.subtitle: Show a model button in the terminal bar and open the model picker with its shortcut (⌥P by default) in agent terminal sessions. Turn off to use terminal bindings.

settings.title: Show session id in terminal panes
settings.subtitle: Show the provider session id in the top-right corner of terminal panes.

settings.title: Editor for ⌃G and $EDITOR prompts
settings.subtitle: Choose which editor ⌃G uses when a terminal prompt asks for $EDITOR.

settings.title: Windows Environment
settings.subtitle: Windows only. PowerShell (default) runs native Windows projects and agents. WSL runs Linux projects. Changing environments prompts you to restart Ghostex.

settings.title: WSL distribution
settings.subtitle: Windows only. Exact distro name from `wsl.exe --list --verbose`; blank uses automatic WSL2 discovery.

settings.title: Scrollback limit
settings.subtitle: Set scrollback memory per terminal surface.

settings.title: Copy on select
settings.subtitle: Copy selected terminal text automatically. On macOS both options also copy to the system clipboard.

settings.title: Confirm close
settings.subtitle: Confirm before closing terminal surfaces.

settings.title: Trim trailing spaces on copy
settings.subtitle: Trim trailing whitespace when copying terminal text.

settings.title: Paste protection
settings.subtitle: Ask before pasting text Ghostty considers unsafe.

settings.title: Paste images as preview links
settings.subtitle: Paste clipboard images as previewable Markdown links with ⌘V. Hold ⌘ over the linked path to preview it in the terminal, and see the same image preview in the ⌃G Rich Prompt Editor.

settings.title: Hide mouse while typing
settings.subtitle: Hide the pointer while typing in the terminal.

settings.title: Scrollbar
settings.subtitle: Control whether Ghostty shows its native scrollback scrollbar.

settings.title: Trackpad scroll speed
settings.subtitle: Trackpads and high-resolution scroll wheels. Ghostty default is 1.

settings.title: Mouse wheel scroll speed
settings.subtitle: Traditional notched mouse wheels. Ghostty default is 3.

settings.title: Scroll to bottom when typing
settings.subtitle: Keep the prompt visible while typing.

settings.title: Show notification on terminal bell
settings.subtitle: Treat terminal bell events as session attention.

settings.title: Agent finished sound
settings.subtitle: The sound when an agent finishes a task or needs you, or Off.

settings.title: System notification when a session needs you
settings.subtitle: Show a system notification when a session needs attention.

settings.title: Alert me for
settings.subtitle: A coordinator's threads finishing, and a coordinator that only finished, stay quiet under both choices, and a red dot (an approval, a stuck or blocked session) always alerts. All plays the finished sound and shows the system notification whenever any other agent finishes; Needs you only does that only when it asks you something, waits for approval, or ends with Blocked or Needs you. The bell keeps every row either way.

settings.title: Finished-work border
settings.subtitle: Outline a session's pane in a colour when its agent finishes work or needs you, until you look at it. The sidebar dot, sounds and notifications stay either way.

settings.title: Finished-work border colour
settings.subtitle: The colour of the border a session's pane gets when its agent finishes work or needs you. Shown while Finished-work border is on.

settings.title: Warn before a banked usage reset expires
settings.subtitle: Show a system notification when a banked Claude or Codex usage reset expires within 3 days and again within 24 hours. The red notification in the bell stays either way.

settings.title: Test alerts
settings.subtitle: Play the agent finished sound and show the notification as they are set now, or open the system's notification settings for Ghostex.

settings.title: Command finished sound
settings.subtitle: The sound when a command run from the Commands pane finishes.

settings.title: Copy sound
settings.subtitle: Play a short sound when copying to the clipboard, including text from the chat composer.

settings.title: HTML, Markdown and images
settings.subtitle: Choose where HTML, Markdown and picture files open from Quick Access, agent chat, the terminal and `ghostex open`: Files, VS Code, the system app (your computer's default app for that file type), or an editor app installed on this computer.

settings.title: Other files
settings.subtitle: Choose where every other file (code and text) opens from Quick Access, agent chat, the terminal and `ghostex open`: Files, VS Code, the system app (your computer's default app for that file type), or an editor app installed on this computer.

settings.title: Videos
settings.subtitle: Choose whether videos linked in agent chat or the terminal, or opened with `ghostex open`, play in Files or open in the system app. Formats Files cannot play, such as .mp4 and .mov, always open in the system app.

settings.title: Open file changes in
settings.subtitle: Choose where Review all on an agent's file changes and Session details' Changes card open: the Changes view or the VS Code view. If the chosen view is turned off, the other one opens.

settings.title: Hide test files in Changes
settings.subtitle: Leave test files (such as foo_test.go, button.test.ts, FooTests.swift and anything in a tests folder) out of the Changes view, so you can review an agent's change without its tests. A line at the top says how many are hidden, with a click to show them. The flask button in the Changes toolbar switches this too.

settings.title: Audio
settings.subtitle: Choose whether audio files linked in agent chat or the terminal, or opened with `ghostex open`, play in Files or open in the system app. Formats Files cannot play, such as .m4a, always open in the system app.

settings.title: Show open files as tabs
settings.subtitle: Show the files open in the Files view as a row of tabs above the document, instead of the Open Files list in the files sidebar. Every file you open, from the files list, Quick Access or a chat link, gets a tab, and each keeps its own unsaved changes and notes.

settings.title: Open links in
settings.subtitle: Open web links from terminal output (Command-click), session chat, and detected dev servers in the project Browser view or the system default browser.

settings.title: Agents open pages in
settings.subtitle: Where an agent opens a page it built for you, such as a website preview: the project Browser view or your default browser. Ask has the agent ask you the first time and save your answer here.

settings.title: Open session links in
settings.subtitle: Open a session's pull requests, issues and Linear tickets (the chips after its title and its links list) in the project Browser view or the system default browser. The phone follows this setting too.

settings.title: Show pages in their own row
settings.subtitle: Show the Browser as one tab in the side panel's tab bar, with its pages as a row of tabs under it, instead of each page as a tab beside the views. Pages open, close, sleep and drag as before.

settings.title: Grok start page
settings.subtitle: The page the Grok view opens on, for every Grok login: grok.com, or a page of your own such as one of your Grok bots. Left empty, or not a web address, it opens grok.com. Shown while the Grok extension is on.

settings.title: Grok logins
settings.subtitle: The Grok logins the bar above the Grok page switches between, each with its own sign-in. Add one there or here; removing one signs it out. Shown while the Grok extension is on.

settings.title: Use VS Code settings
settings.subtitle: Use the VS Code settings from the local VS Code install.

settings.title: Use VS Code Insiders settings
settings.subtitle: Use the VS Code Insiders user settings directory.

settings.title: Open VS Code windows as tabs
settings.subtitle: When VS Code opens a new window (File > New Window, or a folder or workspace opened in a new window), show it as another window tab above the VS Code page instead of blocking it. Each tab is its own VS Code window, so you can keep several projects or workspaces open at once.

settings.title: Detect running servers in terminals
settings.subtitle: Detect localhost dev server URLs from terminal output.

settings.title: Ignored ports
settings.subtitle: Hide detected servers on specific ports or inclusive port ranges.

settings.title: Start Ghostex's server when you log in
settings.subtitle: Runs Ghostex's server in the background from the moment you log in, so your other computers, your phone and coordinators keep working while the app is closed.

settings.title: Also open the Ghostex app
settings.subtitle: Opens the Ghostex window after the server starts at login. Needs Start Ghostex's server when you log in.

settings.title: Resume sessions after a restart or power loss
settings.subtitle: Continues the agent sessions that were running when the computer shut down, restarted or lost power, each in its own chat. Sessions you closed, slept or that had already ended stay as they were. Needs Start Ghostex's server when you log in.

settings.title: Views auto sleep after
settings.subtitle: When inactive VS Code, Git, Project and Browser panes sleep, or Off. Sets the four per-view times below.

settings.title: VS Code sleeps after
settings.subtitle: Choose when inactive VS Code panes sleep, or turn Auto Sleep off. Off also keeps Code awake when more than three views are open.

settings.title: Git sleeps after
settings.subtitle: Choose when inactive Git panes sleep, or turn Auto Sleep off.

settings.title: Project sleeps after
settings.subtitle: Choose when inactive Project panes sleep, or turn Auto Sleep off. Off also keeps Files, Kanban and Automate awake when more than three views are open.

settings.title: Browser sleeps after
settings.subtitle: Choose when inactive browser panes sleep, or turn Auto Sleep off. Off also keeps the Browser awake when more than three views are open.

settings.title: Keep views loaded
settings.subtitle: Keep the side panel views you open loaded when you switch projects or workspaces, without the three-view limit or the previous project's time limit. Auto Sleep and Sleep still apply. Uses more memory.

settings.title: Agents sleep after
settings.subtitle: Choose when eligible agent terminals sleep, or turn Auto Sleep off.

settings.title: Only sleep agents that can be resumed
settings.subtitle: Only auto-sleep agent sessions Ghostex can wake with a resume command.

settings.title: Sleep favourite sessions too
settings.subtitle: Allow favorite agent sessions to auto-sleep.

settings.title: Hide Keep Awake from the sidebar menu
settings.subtitle: Hide the Keep Awake entry from the sidebar menu.

settings.title: Keep Awake lasts
settings.subtitle: Choose the duration Keep Awake uses by default.

settings.title: Let the display sleep while Keep Awake is on
settings.subtitle: Keep the computer awake but allow the display to turn off.

settings.title: Prevent lid-close sleep
settings.subtitle: Optional. When Keep Awake is on, Ghostex can install a small privileged helper once so closing the lid stays awake only for that active keep-awake session.

settings.title: Turn on automatically
settings.subtitle: When Keep Awake turns itself on: when Ghostex launches, when an external display is connected, or while a session is working.

settings.title: Turn off automatically
settings.subtitle: When Keep Awake turns itself off: in Low Power Mode, when this user session is no longer active, or below a battery level.

settings.title: Activate on launch
settings.subtitle: Start preventing sleep when Ghostex launches.

settings.title: Activate on external display
settings.subtitle: Start preventing sleep when an external display is connected.

settings.title: Keep awake for working sessions
settings.subtitle: Keep the computer awake while sessions are working and for 20 minutes after.

settings.title: Battery threshold
settings.subtitle: Stop preventing sleep below this battery level, or turn the rule off.

settings.title: Deactivate in Low Power Mode
settings.subtitle: Stop preventing sleep when Low Power Mode is enabled.

settings.title: Deactivate on user switch
settings.subtitle: Stop preventing sleep when this user session is no longer active.

settings.title: Appearance
settings.subtitle: Follow the system appearance by default, or choose Light or Dark.

settings.title: Dark mode colour
settings.subtitle: The colour of the sidebar and window in dark mode: one of sixteen colour squares, or the + square for a custom colour.

settings.title: Custom dark mode tint
settings.subtitle: The custom dark mode colour, chosen in the colour picker the + square opens.

settings.title: Light mode colour
settings.subtitle: The colour of the sidebar and window in light mode: one of sixteen colour squares, or the + square for a custom colour.

settings.title: Sidebar colourfulness
settings.subtitle: How much of the theme colour shows in the sidebar, from Subtle (deeper, nearly neutral) through Vivid (lighter, more colourful) to Full, which shows the colour you picked itself. Colourfulness sets the sidebar and work area together, and how deep a custom colour is.

settings.title: Work area colourfulness
settings.subtitle: How much of the theme colour shows in the work area (chat, terminals and views), from Subtle to Full. Colourfulness sets the sidebar and work area together.

settings.title: Custom light mode tint
settings.subtitle: The custom light mode colour, chosen in the colour picker the + square opens.

settings.title: App font
settings.subtitle: Pick one of the fonts installed on this computer for the whole app: sidebar, chat, menus, dialogs and Settings, then press Apply. App default keeps Ghostex's own fonts. Terminals and code use the Monospace font.

settings.title: Monospace font
settings.subtitle: Font family for terminals, code in the Files view, diffs, code blocks and tool output in chat. Pick an installed monospace font, or type a Ghostty font-family name, then press Apply.

settings.title: Scale (%)
settings.subtitle: Scale the sidebar, every chat, files open in the Files view and the terminal text together, from 70% to 200%. The header, tabs, menus and dialogs keep their size. Cmd+= and Cmd+- (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) change it from anywhere, and Cmd+0 sets 100%. Default: 100%.

settings.title: Scale areas separately
settings.subtitle: Give the sidebar, chat, Files and terminal text their own sizes instead of one Scale. Cmd+= and Cmd+- then change only the area you are in. Default: off, or on when you had already changed one of those sizes.

settings.title: Sidebar zoom (%)
settings.subtitle: Scale the sidebar, from 50% to 200%, when Scale areas separately is on.

settings.title: Chat zoom (%)
settings.subtitle: Scale every desktop chat, including messages and the prompt composer, from 70% to 200% in 5% steps, when Scale areas separately is on. Cmd+= and Cmd+- in a chat change it too, and Cmd+0 sets 100%. Default: 100%.

settings.title: Files zoom (%)
settings.subtitle: Scale the text of a file open in the Files view (Markdown, text and code, with its line numbers) and the Changes diff, from 70% to 200% in 5% steps, when Scale areas separately is on. Cmd+= and Cmd+- (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) in an open file change it too, and Cmd+0 sets 100%. Default: 100%.

settings.title: Terminal font size
settings.subtitle: The terminal text size in points, when Scale areas separately is on. Cmd+= and Cmd+- in a terminal change it for that terminal only until it restarts. Default: 13.

settings.title: Text strength
settings.subtitle: How strong agents' replies and your messages read in chat, on the computer and the phone. 0% is the standard colour; 100% is full white in dark mode and full black in light mode. Muted text, links, code blocks and status colours stay as they are.

settings.title: Show thinking in grey
settings.subtitle: Show the agent's thinking in grey, so it reads apart from the agent's replies.

settings.title: Chat theme
settings.subtitle: Follow the app theme by default, or override chat with Light, Dark, or System.

settings.title: Terminal theme
settings.subtitle: Follow the app theme by default, or override terminals with Light, Dark, or System.

settings.title: Terminal palette in light mode
settings.subtitle: Uses the light theme set in Ghostex's terminal config, or GitHub Light when none is set.

settings.title: Terminal palette in dark mode
settings.subtitle: Uses the dark theme set in Ghostex's terminal config, or GitHub Dark when none is set.

settings.title: Transparency
settings.subtitle: Let your desktop show through the window: Off, Dark only (light mode stays solid) or Always.

settings.title: Behind the glass
settings.subtitle: Desktop and windows, your wallpaper, a picture you choose, or Live: a calm animation in your theme colours or your own video.

settings.title: Same for light and dark
settings.subtitle: Use the dark-mode picture, video, Live background and tints in light mode too. Turn off to pick them for light mode separately.

settings.title: Picture position
settings.subtitle: Where the wallpaper, custom picture or your own Live video sits behind the glass. Stays with the desktop can trail the window while you drag it.

settings.title: Picture for dark mode
settings.subtitle: The picture the glass blurs in dark mode when Picture shows behind the glass.

settings.title: Picture for light mode
settings.subtitle: The picture the glass blurs in light mode when Picture shows behind the glass.

settings.title: Your video for dark mode
settings.subtitle: The video file the glass plays in dark mode when Live is set to Your video.

settings.title: Your video for light mode
settings.subtitle: The video file the glass plays in light mode when Live is set to Your video.

settings.title: Play only when plugged in
settings.subtitle: Pause the Live animation or video while your computer runs on battery. It always pauses when Ghostex is in the background.

settings.title: Live background for dark mode
settings.subtitle: The animation, or your own video, the glass shows in dark mode when Live shows behind the glass.

settings.title: Live background for light mode
settings.subtitle: The animation, or your own video, the glass shows in light mode when Live shows behind the glass.

settings.title: Live background speed
settings.subtitle: How fast the Live animation moves, from a quarter of its pace to twice as fast.

settings.title: Live background brightness
settings.subtitle: How bright the Live animation glows behind the glass. Lower keeps it a subtle glow.

settings.title: Blur
settings.subtitle: How soft what shows behind the window looks, in points. 0 shows it sharp. On Windows and Linux, Desktop and windows uses the system blur, so this sets the wallpaper, picture and video blur; on Windows, Blur on Windows picks that system blur.
settings.availability: Not shown on Windows while Behind the glass is Desktop and windows.

settings.title: Blur on Windows
settings.subtitle: How Windows blurs what shows behind the window while Desktop and windows shows behind the glass. Windows has no blur amount to set, so pick Acrylic (Windows' own frosted blur), Plain blur (the same blur without Windows' grey frost, so the tints can go fully clear; it takes more work to draw) or Off (sharp, the fastest).

settings.title: Menu blur
settings.subtitle: How soft what shows behind menus, panels, dialogs and tooltips looks, in points. Menus, panels and dialogs blur a quarter more than this number; tooltips use it as is. 0 shows it sharp.

settings.title: Sidebar tint in dark mode
settings.subtitle: How much of the desktop the sidebar hides in dark mode. Lower shows more of your desktop through it.

settings.title: Work area tint in dark mode
settings.subtitle: How much of the desktop the work area hides in dark mode, set on its own so either area can be the darker one. Lower shows more of your desktop through it.

settings.title: Sidebar tint in light mode
settings.subtitle: How much of the desktop the sidebar hides in light mode. Lower shows more of your desktop through it.

settings.title: Work area tint in light mode
settings.subtitle: How much of the desktop the work area hides in light mode, set on its own so either area can be the darker one. Lower shows more of your desktop through it.

settings.title: Show active pane outline
settings.subtitle: Show an outline around the currently focused pane.

settings.title: Active pane outline colour
settings.subtitle: Color of the outline around the currently focused pane.

settings.title: Frame the work area
settings.subtitle: Show the work area as a card inside the window, with a thin margin all around, a hairline border and a light shadow. Off keeps the work area edge to edge.

settings.title: Show the window buttons when the sidebar is collapsed
settings.subtitle: Keep the red, yellow and green window buttons in the window's top left while the sidebar is collapsed. Off hides them until you open the floating sidebar, which carries them in its top row. Full screen keeps its own title bar either way.

settings.title: Display scale
settings.subtitle: Linux only. How big the whole app is drawn: the header, menus, dialogs and web pages too. Automatic follows your desktop's display scale; pick a fixed one if Ghostex gets it wrong. Interface scale applies on top. Takes effect when Ghostex restarts. Default: Automatic.

settings.title: Pane gap
settings.subtitle: Gap in pixels between split panes in the Agents view.

settings.title: Custom dark mode depth (set by Colourfulness)
settings.subtitle: How deep the custom dark mode colour is. Colourfulness sets it whenever it moves; it has no control of its own.

settings.title: Custom light mode depth (set by Colourfulness)
settings.subtitle: How deep the custom light mode colour is. Colourfulness sets it whenever it moves; it has no control of its own.

settings.title: Sidebar foreground color (derived)
settings.subtitle: Derived from Background Contrast and Background Tint; change those instead.

settings.title: Sidebar background color (derived)
settings.subtitle: Derived from Background Contrast and Background Tint; change those instead.

settings.title: Update all
settings.subtitle: Updates everything the shown machine lists that has an update (Update all machines, beside the machine picker, updates every connected machine): the agents you use, Claude Swap and Codex Swap, Fast Computer & Browser Use, SpaceO, the tools Ghostex installed, extensions, remote machines, the VS Code view and the Chromium runtime. Ghostex itself updates last and restarts once; your agents keep running, and each agent whose CLI changed restarts into the same chat once it finishes its turn.

settings.title: Update automatically
settings.subtitle: A switch on each card, off by default: Ghostex installs that item's updates by itself, only while it isn't in use (an agent while none of its sessions is working, the other tools while no agent is working). On Ghostex's own card it is Keep this machine up to date.

settings.title: Check now
settings.subtitle: Checks every item for a newer version now instead of waiting for the next check (every half hour).

settings.title: Up to date
settings.subtitle: Everything already current, and the agents Ghostex can't read the version of (such as Cursor), with a button that runs their own updater.

settings.title: Show debug UI controls
settings.subtitle: Show diagnostic logs. From the next start, also opens Chromium's DevTools port (9334) for developer tools.

settings.title: Diagnostic logs
settings.subtitle: Pick the areas to log while you reproduce an issue, and when logging turns off. Warnings, errors, and crashes are always captured.

settings.title: Track Claude without its hooks
settings.subtitle: Follow Claude sessions' activity and conversation from the session files Claude writes itself instead of from its hooks. The hooks stay installed and are only compared.

settings.title: Version
settings.subtitle: Ghostex app version.

settings.title: Join Discord
settings.subtitle: Chat with the community and get help.

settings.title: View on GitHub
settings.subtitle: View the source, releases, and report issues.

settings.title: Sponsor Ghostex
settings.subtitle: Support the continued development of Ghostex.

settings.title: Anonymous analytics
settings.subtitle: Send anonymous usage analytics. Ask the user before changing it.

settings.title: gpuiTitlebarActionCommandByProject
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: gpuiTitlebarOpenTargetByProject
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: agentsTidyUpOfferDismissed
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: sessionLinksFoldedGroups
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: settingsModalNavigation
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: projectWebsiteViews
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: appIconSourceId
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: unifiedProjectOrder
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: customSidebarTitlebarLightBackgroundColor
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: hotkeys
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: customViewTemplates
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: viewScopes
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: customWorkspaceOpenTargets
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: workspaceOpenTargetAvailability
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: workspaceOpenTargetHiddenIds
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: remoteMachines
settings.subtitle: App-managed state saved with the settings; not a user preference.

settings.title: Terminal Action
settings.subtitle: Add terminal actions to run saved commands in quick command terminals with one click or a hotkey.

settings.title: Browser Action
settings.subtitle: Add browser actions to open saved URLs in browser panes.

settings.title: Custom actions
settings.subtitle: Actions are custom shortcuts for repeat work, shared between a main project and its worktrees.

settings.title: Global Actions
settings.subtitle: Global actions apply to every project, are stored by the Ghostex daemon, and appear under Global in every project's Start menu.

settings.title: Accounts, usage stats and automatic continuation
settings.subtitle: Current CLI login, Claude cswap, Codex xswap, add account, Cursor, Gemini and Copilot usage, reconnect, sign in again, use this account automatically, only when I pick it, or paused, update, reinstall or uninstall Claude Swap and Codex Swap, show usage in the sidebar, status lines, usage limits and resets (5h, 7d, Mo), session badges, account numbers, auto-switch, new sessions start on, when an account hits its limit, hide emails, privacy, error recovery and retry settings.

settings.title: Account usage in the sidebar
settings.subtitle: Show or hide usage stats for saved Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Copilot accounts at the bottom of the desktop sidebar. Adding an account pins the usage there.

settings.title: Auto-redeem expiring Claude resets
settings.subtitle: Ghostex automatically uses a banked Claude reset 5 minutes before it expires, so it isn't lost.

settings.title: Also use expiring Claude resets at a limit
settings.subtitle: When you hit a Claude usage limit and a banked reset expires within 24 hours, Ghostex automatically uses it right away instead of waiting for its last 5 minutes. Needs Auto-redeem expiring Claude resets.

settings.title: Auto-redeem expiring Codex resets
settings.subtitle: Ghostex automatically uses a banked Codex reset 5 minutes before it expires, so it isn't lost.

settings.title: Also use expiring Codex resets at a limit
settings.subtitle: When you hit a Codex usage limit and a banked reset expires within 24 hours, Ghostex automatically uses it right away instead of waiting for its last 5 minutes. Needs Auto-redeem expiring Codex resets.

settings.title: Hide account emails
settings.subtitle: Hide account email addresses in the Accounts page and account switchers.

settings.title: Autopilot
settings.subtitle: Keep sessions going while you are away: carry on a session that stopped while its background job finished or mid-task, interrupt one stuck on a hung command, reload one that stays frozen, move one at a usage limit to an account with room, restart one whose terminal ended. Stays on until you turn it off. Also from a coordinator's chat (its Autopilot pill) and ghostex autopilot on|off.

settings.title: Which sessions
settings.subtitle: Every session, only the projects you pick (and their worktrees), or only sessions you pick one by one. A session's Autopilot pill in its chat takes it out or puts it back; a project's right-click menu, Advanced > Autopilot, does the same for the project and its worktrees.

settings.title: What it may do on its own
settings.subtitle: Heal (carry on, interrupt, reload, switch account), Heal and decide (also answer with the recommended choice), or Everything (also approve any prompt that is not a hard limit).

settings.title: Hard limits it may cross
settings.subtitle: Each off until you turn it on: push a branch, finish a release you asked for, push main, merge pull requests, delete outside the project, post publicly. Sign-ins, 2FA, identity checks and payments are never done.

settings.title: Answer questions for me
settings.subtitle: After waiting 5, 10 or 15 minutes for you, pick each question's recommended choice. Off by default.

settings.title: Answer approval cards
settings.subtitle: Answer approval cards (permission prompts, Connectors cards, folder trust) within what it may do. Off by default: only your click answers them.

settings.title: Supervisor model
settings.subtitle: The agent that wakes for judgment calls: Claude Opus 5.5 at medium, or Codex GPT 6.1 Sol at high. It starts on an account with room.

settings.title: Look at every session every
settings.subtitle: How often Autopilot sweeps every session it covers, from 1 to 10 minutes (2 by default). A session whose turn ends is looked at right away.

settings.title: Summary and log
settings.subtitle: Every decision Autopilot made, newest first: the session, what it saw, what it did, and what happened. Kept 30 days. Also ghostex autopilot log.

settings.title: Ghostex Collab
settings.subtitle: Collab is installed on this computer (Settings > Extensions installs it, with Touch ID or your system's equivalent; this page shows only once it is). Share is in each chat's header, and each share asks for your approval. Uninstall ends every share at once and removes Collab from this computer; it never asks.

settings.title: Your name
settings.subtitle: The name guests see for you ("Shared by …", "Waiting for …"). Empty uses this computer's user name.

settings.title: Guest messages
settings.subtitle: What a guest's message does: Ask me (you approve each one with Send, Edit or Decline), Send (straight to the agent, labelled with their name) or View only. Ask me by default; change it for one chat in its Share popover.

settings.title: Link ends after
settings.subtitle: 1 hour (the default), 4 hours, 24 hours, or Until I stop it (the link stays live until you stop sharing). Stop sharing, or deleting the chat, ends a link at once. The Share popover's chip changes it too.

settings.title: Ask for a code
settings.subtitle: Guests also type the six-digit code shown in the Share popover, so a link alone is not enough. On by default.

settings.title: Shared chats
settings.subtitle: Every chat shared right now, how many are watching it and when its link ends, with Stop sharing for each and Stop all.

settings.title: Guest messages log
settings.subtitle: Every message guests sent to a shared chat and what happened to it (went straight to the agent, waited for you, sent, edited or declined), and who joined, left or was removed, newest first.

settings.title: Turn agents on or off
settings.subtitle: Turn on the agents you use; they appear in the New session menu, the sidebar's Select Agent and on your phone. Drag to set their order. Agents you turned off but used before stay dimmed in the list; agents you never used wait under More agents. Expand a row to edit its command, permission mode and default view, or to install or update its CLI.

settings.title: Add custom agent
settings.subtitle: Add your own command, or a variant of a built-in agent with other flags. Works like gives it that agent's logo, chat view, resume hook and permission handling. Custom agents can be turned off or deleted.

settings.title: Default view per agent
settings.subtitle: Agents that support Ghostex's Chat View are marked with a chat bubble and can open in Chat or Terminal regardless of the global Default Agent View. Inherit keeps following that global setting.

settings.title: Remember the agent you pick
settings.subtitle: Which agent a project's new-session button (and New Agent Session) starts: the one you last picked in that project, in its Space, or one choice for every project. A project with no pick yet starts the agent you picked last.

settings.title: Default Prompt Agent
settings.subtitle: Choose the agent used by Git helper prompts, project board Start Work, and the default worktree first-prompt selection.

settings.title: Title Generation Agent
settings.subtitle: Choose the headless agent Ghostex uses for first-prompt session title generation. Hover the info icon to see the exact command Ghostex sends.

settings.title: Custom Title Command
settings.subtitle: Run this command with the title prompt on stdin. It should print only the title.

settings.title: Agent approvals
settings.subtitle: Choose whether supported agents ask before editing files or running commands. Per-agent settings can override this default.

settings.title: Trust project folders automatically
settings.subtitle: Mark each project and worktree folder as trusted before its agent starts, so no session stops at a "Do you trust this folder?" prompt. Turn it off to answer that prompt yourself.

settings.title: Agent approvals: accept all
settings.subtitle: Start supported agents with approvals turned off (full access) by default. Off keeps each agent CLI default approval mode. Projects can override it.

settings.title: Default Prompt Agent
settings.subtitle: Agent id used when Ghostex sends a prompt on your behalf (for example PR review). Use an id from the configured agents.

settings.title: Title Generation Agent
settings.subtitle: Headless agent Ghostex uses for first-prompt session title generation.

settings.title: Custom Title Command
settings.subtitle: Custom command run with the title prompt on stdin when Title Generation Agent is custom. It should print only the title.

settings.title: Session resume hooks
settings.subtitle: Hooks let Ghostex capture each agent's native session id and resume the exact conversation after sleep, reload, or app restart. Install one agent's hook from its row, fix every agent that is on with Fix all, install every missing hook with Install all (shown only when a hook is missing), or remove every Ghostex hook with Uninstall all in the ⋯ menu.

settings.title: Install the hook when I turn on an agent
settings.subtitle: Install an agent's session resume hook as soon as you turn it on, without asking.

settings.title: Show Main Hub on all Spaces
settings.subtitle: Show Main Hub and your home folder's sessions at the top of every Space. Off, they stay at the top of the Space you moved them to.

settings.title: Ask before New Chat
settings.subtitle: Ask before New Chat or Change Agent starts a new chat with Chief of Staff. Your earlier chats stay in Main Hub either way.

settings.title: Chief of Staff may add GBots on its own
settings.subtitle: With GBots on, Chief of Staff adds a GBot when a job needs one and tells you in a card you can undo. Off, it asks you before adding each one. Only you can change this, not an agent.

settings.title: Folders agents can't read in your home folder
settings.subtitle: Agents Ghostex starts in your home folder are kept out of these folders and files. Claude Code's file tools and every Codex command are held to the list; Claude's shell commands and other agents are not.

settings.title: Floating Capture
settings.subtitle: A small button that floats over every app and shows how many agents are working, waiting for you, or asking a question. Screenshot an area, an app or the whole screen, mark it up, and send a prompt to any project or session without switching to Ghostex. Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+S (Alt+Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux) opens it; A, Space, F or T instead of S capture an area, the current app or the full screen, or write a prompt, right away.

settings.title: Ghostex CLI
settings.subtitle: Ghostex keeps the app-bundled ghostex command linked automatically for mobile apps and CLI-backed integration setup.

settings.title: Bundled Agent Skills
settings.subtitle: Install the Ghostex skills you want agents to discover. Ghostex Computer Use and Ghostex Browser Use need Fast Computer & Browser Use installed first and also install its cua-driver skill, and Ghostex SpaceO needs SpaceO (Mac only). Each Ghostex skill is copied to ~/.agents/skills and can be updated or uninstalled independently, or removed together with Uninstall All.

settings.title: Fast Computer & Browser Use Permissions
settings.subtitle: Fast Computer & Browser Use needs Accessibility to click and type in apps, and Screen Recording to understand what is visible on the desktop.

settings.title: SpaceO
settings.subtitle: On an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 or later, install SpaceO so agents can use Mac apps on their own hidden screen while you keep your own screen, pointer and focus. Ghostex runs the official installer, keeps SpaceO running in the background, and installs the Ghostex SpaceO skill; once installed, update, reinstall or uninstall it from the same row.

settings.title: SpaceO Permissions
settings.subtitle: SpaceO needs Accessibility to click and type in apps, and Screen Recording to take screenshots of the apps it runs.

settings.title: Tools
settings.subtitle: Install, update, reinstall or uninstall the tools Ghostex sets up for you: Node.js and npm, uv, Homebrew, Linux system tools, Beads, and the GitHub and GitLab CLIs. Each Install button says how it installs; your own copies are used when you have them.

settings.title: Chromium runtime (CEF)
settings.subtitle: Install, reinstall or uninstall the optional web runtime used by the Browser, the VS Code view, website and extension views, and HTML files in Files. It also installs from the first view that needs it.

settings.title: Show the floating button
settings.subtitle: Show the Floating Capture button over every app: agent counts, screenshots of an area, an app or the whole screen, and quick prompts without switching to Ghostex.

settings.title: Switch to the session after sending
settings.subtitle: After a prompt is sent from Floating Capture, the Ghostex window shows the session it went to, without coming in front of the app you are in.

settings.title: Instabox
settings.subtitle: Connect your Instabox.sh account in the browser, or paste an API key. Boxes run on your account and bill to it.

settings.title: Boat
settings.subtitle: Connect your Boat.dev account: Ghostex asks for your email, opens Boat's page and shows a 6-digit code to type there. Or paste an API key.

settings.title: This month
settings.subtitle: What your Cloud Boxes cost this month, per provider and in total. Instabox counts everything on that account; Boat counts the boxes Ghostex made.

settings.title: Monthly cap
settings.subtitle: Ghostex warns at 80% of this many dollars a month and starts no new box at 100%. Running boxes keep running. 0 turns the cap off.

settings.title: Stop idle boxes after
settings.subtitle: A box with no agent working and no terminal open pauses (Instabox) or stops (Boat) after this long. Sending a message wakes it.

settings.title: Delete archived boxes after
settings.subtitle: When every session on a box is archived, the box stops and is deleted after this many days. A box with unpushed work is kept until you push or delete it.

settings.title: Start boxes from your phone
settings.subtitle: Keep your provider key, agent logins, Default snapshots and picked secrets on your paired phones, so they can start a box while this computer is off.

settings.title: Your boxes
settings.subtitle: Every box with its state, project, age and cost. Stop a box, or delete it; a box with unpushed work asks first.

settings.title: Claude on cloud boxes
settings.subtitle: Allow a Claude account on boxes: it makes a one-year box token after one approval in your browser, so Claude on this computer stays signed in.

settings.title: Codex on cloud boxes
settings.subtitle: Allow a Codex account on boxes: each box gets a fresh copy of its login and sends refreshed sign-ins back to this computer.

settings.title: agentbox
settings.subtitle: Install agentbox, the free open-source command line tool Ghostex uses to run agent sessions in boxes, see its version and whether Docker is running, and run its check.

settings.title: Set it up for me
settings.subtitle: Start an agent that installs agentbox, asks which clouds you want, creates the API tokens in your browser, and signs Claude and Codex in for boxes.

settings.title: What is a box?
settings.subtitle: A box is an isolated copy of your project where an agent works without touching this computer. Your agent's settings, skills and Codex sign-in go with it, and its web app opens on this computer.

settings.title: Where boxes run
settings.subtitle: Set up Docker on this computer, or log in to a cloud provider with an API token and prepare its base image once. Cloud boxes bill while they exist.

settings.title: Your own server (SSH)
settings.subtitle: Add your own server with Docker by a name and its SSH address (user@host or a name from ~/.ssh/config), then check that boxes can run there.

settings.title: Claude in boxes
settings.subtitle: Claude needs its own one-time sign-in for boxes, so Claude on this computer stays signed in. Every box uses it.

settings.title: Codex in boxes
settings.subtitle: Boxes on this computer reuse your Codex sign-in. Sign in here for cloud boxes when Codex is not signed in.

settings.title: Default location
settings.subtitle: Where new threads run unless you pick another location.

settings.title: Your boxes
settings.subtitle: See every box, open a box's web app, stop a box, or destroy it to delete it for good.

settings.title: Start a thread in an agentbox box
settings.subtitle: Open New Thread and pick where it runs under Run on. Boxes open in the terminal view.

settings.title: Open a box's web app
settings.subtitle: Right-click the session and choose Open Box Web App to open it on this computer. Add an agentbox.yaml with services.web.expose.port to start your dev server in the box automatically.

settings.title: Cloud boxes bill until stopped
settings.subtitle: Cloud providers charge while a box exists. Deleting a session stops its box and keeps its work; Destroy removes the box.

settings.title: Arrange views
settings.subtitle: Reorder built-in, extension, and custom views. New tabs open in this order, and ⌥1 through ⌥9 follow the tabs in the view panel.

settings.title: Hide VS Code view
settings.subtitle: Stop offering the VS Code view, so it is missing from the view panel tab strip, its + menu and the view picker.

settings.title: Hide Browser view
settings.subtitle: Stop offering the Browser view, so it is missing from the view panel tab strip, its + menu and the view picker.

settings.title: Hide Kanban view

settings.title: Executor

settings.title: Executor apps

settings.title: Sign-in callback address
settings.subtitle: The address to give an app's developer console when it needs your own sign-in app (OAuth client).

settings.title: Ask, Allow or Never
settings.subtitle: What a workspace does before an agent sends, posts, creates, changes or deletes something through a connector: ask on a card, allow it, or never run it.

settings.title: Rules for one tool
settings.subtitle: The tools set to always allow or never run, for example after Always allow on a card.

settings.title: GitHub CLI and Google Workspace CLI
settings.subtitle: Each workspace's own gh and gws sign-in, which agents started there use.

settings.title: Engine
settings.subtitle: Which service turns your recording into text: Hex, a free dictation app that runs on this computer with no key and works offline (macOS on Apple silicon, Windows, Linux), or OpenAI or xAI with your API key. Hex is recommended; Set up Hex installs it and walks you through it. A new install picks your saved key (xAI, then OpenAI) and Hex when there is no key; after that it stays on what you pick. Each computer has its own engine, and the phone changes it per computer.

settings.title: OpenAI API key
settings.subtitle: Shown under the engine when it is OpenAI: paste your key from platform.openai.com. It is the same key the Voice Agent uses on GPT Realtime, kept encrypted on this computer.

settings.title: xAI API key
settings.subtitle: Shown under the engine when it is xAI: paste your key from console.x.ai. It is the same key the Voice Agent uses on Grok Voice, kept encrypted on this computer.

settings.title: Old speech models
settings.subtitle: The models Ghostex's own speech engine downloaded before Hex replaced it. Ghostex no longer uses them; Delete frees the space.

settings.title: Language
settings.subtitle: Auto works for most people. Pick one when short phrases come out in the wrong language.

settings.title: Hotkey
settings.subtitle: Dictate into the chat box you are in. Change it in Hotkeys.

settings.title: Hotkey mode
settings.subtitle: Auto: tap to start and tap again to stop, or hold for 300 ms or more and it stops when you let go. Toggle: every press starts or stops. Hold: it records only while you hold the keys. Escape cancels.

settings.title: Microphone
settings.subtitle: The microphone this computer records dictation from. System default follows the input device chosen in your sound settings.

settings.title: Dictionary
settings.subtitle: Names and terms it should expect. An alias fixes a word it keeps mishearing ("GX server" becomes gxserver). Your project names are added on their own.

settings.title: Remove filler words
settings.subtitle: Drops "um", "uh" and other hesitation sounds.

settings.title: Insert with spacing
settings.subtitle: Adds a space before or after the text when the characters next to the caret need one.

settings.title: AI polish
settings.subtitle: Claude Sonnet 5.5 fixes punctuation and keeps what you meant when you corrected yourself ("no, I mean…"), through Claude Code on the computer that transcribes. The chat box shows Polishing with a Skip button; if it fails, the text goes in unpolished.

settings.title: Dictation history
settings.subtitle: Every recording you made with the dictation microphone, newest first, with its text and the engine that made it. Play, download or delete a recording, copy its text, recover one you cancelled, or transcribe one that failed (the text is copied to your clipboard too). Recordings stay on this computer until you delete them.

settings.title: Voice provider
settings.subtitle: Which realtime voice model you talk to: xAI Grok Voice or OpenAI GPT Realtime. Both are billed by the provider while a conversation is open. It doesn't follow Dictation's engine: dictation can stay on Hex while calls use xAI or OpenAI.

settings.title: xAI API key
settings.subtitle: Shown under the provider when it is xAI Grok Voice. Dictation uses the same key when its engine is xAI. Kept encrypted on this computer; your phone uses it through this computer and never stores it. With a 1Password account added in Settings > Secrets, paste an op://vault/item/field reference instead and the key is read from 1Password each time.

settings.title: OpenAI API key
settings.subtitle: Shown under the provider when it is OpenAI GPT Realtime. Dictation uses the same key when its engine is OpenAI. Kept encrypted on this computer and never shown again after you save it. With a 1Password account added in Settings > Secrets, paste an op://vault/item/field reference instead.

settings.title: Grok voice
settings.subtitle: The voice Grok Voice speaks with.

settings.title: OpenAI voice
settings.subtitle: The voice GPT Realtime speaks with. Marin and Cedar sound the most natural.

settings.title: Speaking speed
settings.subtitle: How fast the voice agent talks, from normal speed to twice as fast. The voice keeps its pitch, and the speed menu next to the voice in the voice panel changes it too, even mid-sentence.

settings.title: Call mode
settings.subtitle: Regular calls listen hands-free; on Grok they're billed for the whole time the call is connected, quiet and muted time included (about $0.08 a minute). Push-to-talk calls listen only while you hold the talk button next to Mute (or Space, or the Hold to Talk hotkey); on Grok you pay only for the audio you send and the agent's replies. In a muted Regular call, holding it unmutes you for as long as you hold. GPT Realtime bills only audio in both modes. A change applies to your next call; the gear in the voice panel changes it too.

settings.title: Last conversation
settings.subtitle: A short summary of your last voice conversation, kept on this computer until the next conversation replaces it. Press Continue in the voice panel, or say "pick up where we left off", to carry on from it. Forget deletes it.

settings.title: Expand collapsed projects on jump
settings.subtitle: Expand a collapsed project when a project-jump hotkey lands on it.

settings.title: Skip sleeping sessions
settings.subtitle: Next Session and Previous Session jump over sleeping sessions in the sidebar.
